Tool Calling

You might say

AI can talk, but how do I get it to actually check the database or make a request?

A model’s request for an application to run a named tool with parameters·A model can request a calendar lookup, but the application must validate the permissions and parameters before it reads the schedule. The returned result, not the request text, proves what happened.
Know first

Function Calling

User asks
Can you check whether I’m free tomorrow afternoon?
How a tool request becomes a real result

Request execution based on tool definitions: Tools are defined with a name, description, and typed parameters. The model fills parameters to request a tool call, but this is only an invocation request—the model does not run the tool directly.

The application validates permissions and parameters: It checks whether the tool is permitted, whether parameters make sense, and whether the user has access.

Real execution results return to the model: Only the executed result from the external tool comes back to the model to formulate the final answer.

What people often confuse

Data-shaped parameters are not permission to act. Delete and send actions still need scope checks and confirmation.

You can say this to an AI Agent

“

Validate meeting creation with a mock or dedicated test calendar, not a real schedule. Show the proposed time, attendees, and title before the call; simulate one success and one permission denial, reporting only from the actual tool result. Delete any event created in the test calendar afterward.

You might say

**A model’s request for an application to run a named tool with parameters**·A model can request a calendar lookup, but the application must validate the permissions and parameters before it reads the schedule. The returned result, not the request text, proves what happened.

How a tool request becomes a real result

**Request execution based on tool definitions:**Tools are defined with a name, description, and typed parameters. The model fills parameters to request a tool call, but this is only an invocation request—the model does not run the tool directly.

**The application validates permissions and parameters:**It checks whether the tool is permitted, whether parameters make sense, and whether the user has access.

**Real execution results return to the model:**Only the executed result from the external tool comes back to the model to formulate the final answer.
**What people often confuse**
Data-shaped parameters are not permission to act. Delete and send actions still need scope checks and confirmation.

## You can say this to an AI Agent

> “
> Validate meeting creation with a mock or dedicated test calendar, not a real schedule. Show the proposed time, attendees, and title before the call; simulate one success and one permission denial, reporting only from the actual tool result. Delete any event created in the test calendar afterward.
